view: Macro has turned from a mild headwind into a clear headwind for a long-duration mega-cap. Markets moved into broad risk-off (VIX 35.9, ES -8.55% on the week, Nasdaq about -10%, SOX -17.13%, S5TH 45.92, HY OAS 3.52 and widening), and there is no Fed put: CPI is 3.7 against Fed funds 4.0, Oct PPI YoY is 6.5, and Fed speakers are talking about hikes. Unlike last week, a shared market and sector factor explains roughly 40-75% of NVDA's -22.92% week. Rates are not what drove it: the 10y fell to 4.95 as money moved to safety. Growth and credit levels (ISM 55.5, NFCI -0.48) are not yet recessionary, so this looks like a de-rating of the AI complex in a hawkish setting, not a systemic crisis.

probabilities.defs: 2w ±5%, quarters ±10%, vs price_at_call 125.53 (Fri 2026-11-20 close, weekend run). next_2_weeks: up = close > 131.81, down = close < 119.25, range between, measured at the close on or before 2026-12-06 (i.e. Fri 2026-12-04, NFP day). this_quarter: to the last close of 2026-12-31; next_quarter: to the last close of 2027-03-31; up > 138.08, down < 112.98, range between. up + range + down = 100.

evidence.point: Outside view 33/45/22 (n=259). Moved to 35/29/36: up +2, range -16, down +14. Main reason: a volatility regime far above the sample norm (VIX 35.9; NVDA -14.01% in one session, and one-day moves of -10% or worse occur on only 0.24% of past days), which drains the ±5% range bucket. The two tails are nearly equal. Capitulation-style readings (Nasdaq worst week since Mar 2020; conditional 2w drop <=-15% n=4: 50/50/0) support a rebound. Against that, no Fed easing is available and credit is starting to widen. The conditional samples are tiny and overlapping, so they are weak evidence.

Base 39/43/18. Moved to 34/32/34 (up -5, range -11, down +16). The macro part of the move is that FOMC 2026-12-09 and CPI 2026-12-10 (fcst 3.9 vs prev 3.7) fall inside the window while Fed speakers discuss hikes. A hawkish surprise during a VIX-35 risk-off would hit high-beta duration hardest. The remaining extra down weight reflects the SEC/accounting tail, which is outside my lane.

Base 50/31/19. Moved to 42/24/34 (up -8, range -7, down +15). The conditional rates (RSI<=36 n=13: 69% up, median +21.5%; 2w drop <=-15% n=4: 100% up, median +32.1%) point up, but neither sample contains a hiking Fed together with a market-wide risk-off. ISM 55.5 and a positive curve rule out a recession base case, which keeps the up bucket the largest.

VIX 35.9 (+26.28% on the day). ES -8.55% on the week, SPX -3.7% on Friday, Nasdaq Comp -5.28% on Friday. This is now a market-wide risk-off regime, not a stock-specific shock. High VIX levels have usually been followed by mean reversion, but the path is wide in both directions.

S5TH 45.92 (chg -3.18): fewer than half of S&P 500 members are above their 200d, so breadth has broken below 50. This is a broad deterioration, not just a rotation away from mega-caps. RSP/SPY was not displayed in the panel this run, so I cannot say whether equal-weight is still outperforming. Unknown, not neutral.

HY OAS 3.52 (chg +0.05): credit is widening, but only modestly against a VIX of 35.9. NFCI -0.48 (a weekly, lagging series) still shows loose conditions. Equities are under stress and credit is not yet: a headwind that is not systemic. Contagion would show as HY OAS moving toward 4 or higher with NFCI rising toward zero.

CPI YoY 3.7 vs Fed funds 4.0 (a real policy rate of only about 0.3). Oct PPI YoY is 6.5, pipeline inflation running hot. fed_context: per Reuters 2026-11-13, markets still expect more hikes, and Musalem wants several hikes before spring. The Fed cannot cushion an equity drawdown, which is the main macro headwind for the quarter buckets.

Real 10y 2.88, nominal 10y 4.95 (chg -0.10), 30y 5.337, TLT 81.45. Money moved into Treasuries during the selloff, so the nominal discount rate eased slightly. Real rates are still restrictive for long-duration equity. This week's damage did not come from rates.
Curve positive (10y-3m 0.6, 10y-2y 0.29): there is no inversion-style recession signal. Neutral for growth.
ISM PMI 55.5, new orders 55.5: the real economy is expanding, which supports AI-capex demand. Inflation is the constraint, not growth.
DXY 103.84 and USDJPY 158.556 are minor headwinds. A sharp yen rally from here would signal forced deleveraging, a watch item only.

Attribution: NVDA -22.92% for the week vs SPX -8.61%, SOX -17.13%, Nasdaq about -10%. On Friday NVDA fell -14.01% vs SOX -10.73%, AMD -13.25% and SPX -3.7%. At beta 1, the market factor explains about 38% of the week; the sector factor (SOX) explains about 75%; the residual vs SOX is about -5.8 pts. Beta is not in the slice. Caveat: NVDA is a large SOX and Nasdaq weight with a market cap of 3.03T, so part of the 'common factor' is NVDA itself (reflexive). Macro in the rates/inflation sense explains little. Risk appetite for the AI complex explains most of it. Over 1m, NVDA is -43.19%; an SPX 1m figure is not in the slice.

Dated catalysts inside the 2w window: 2026-11-25 GDP Q3 2nd est, core PCE, income/spending, durables (a hot core PCE is the first test of the hike narrative); 2026-11-26 Thanksgiving closed; 2026-11-27 half-day (thin liquidity at high VIX); 2026-12-01 ISM mfg (prev 55.5) plus a requested Huang House interview; 2026-12-02 NVDA ex-dividend; 2026-12-03 ISM services plus a requested Senate hearing; 2026-12-04 NFP, which is also the 2w measurement close. In the quarter window: 2026-12-09 FOMC, 2026-12-10 CPI (fcst 3.9, prev 3.7), 2026-12-15 PPI. A retail sales date inside the window is not in the slice.

Coverage 7/14 ok. My core page tv_purple_list is ok (read after event_cutoff 2026-11-20T21:00Z), but RSP/SPY, IC4WSA claims and the liquidity composite were not displayed, so breadth rests on S5TH alone. tv_relative is partial: there are no SMH/AVGO/TSM weekly figures, so the sector attribution relies on SOX and AMD's daily move only. options_positioning is deferred, so dealer gamma around a VIX-35 market is unknown, not neutral. Confidence is lowered for these gaps.

key_levels.why: Capitulation-day low (Fri 2026-11-20). In a VIX-35 tape, a close below it means the forced selling has not finished.
VIX; a fall back toward 25 would mark the risk-off phase easing. A rise above 40 would mean systemic stress.
HY OAS; widening toward 4.0 would turn an equity de-rating into a credit event
Real 10y; still restrictive. A hawkish FOMC or CPI pushing it up would deepen the duration headwind.
S5TH; a fall toward 40 or lower means breadth is still breaking down. Back above 50 means repair.

what_would_change_my_mind: More bullish (2w and quarter): core PCE on 2026-11-25 at or below expectations, VIX closing below 25 by 2026-12-04, and HY OAS back below 3.4 with S5TH back above 50.
More bullish (quarter buckets): CPI on 2026-12-10 at or below 3.7 (vs 3.9 fcst) and the FOMC on 2026-12-09 holding without a hiking bias, with real 10y below 2.80.
More bearish: HY OAS above 4.0 with NFCI rising above -0.30 before 2026-12-31 (risk-off turning into a credit event).
More bearish: the FOMC on 2026-12-09 hikes or signals several hikes, with CPI on 2026-12-10 at or above 3.9 and 30y back above 5.5.
More bearish: ISM manufacturing on 2026-12-01 below 52 or a negative NFP on 2026-12-04. A growth scare on top of hot inflation is a stagflation mix with no Fed relief.

Expected line (not a trigger): the 2026-11-25 data, the Thanksgiving half-day, NFP 2026-12-04 (the 2w measurement day), FOMC 2026-12-09 and CPI 2026-12-10 will all happen. Only their outcomes, phrased above, move my view.
notes_for_chair: Update vs my 2026-11-15 submission (32/35/33, 35/36/29, 44/27/29 at 162.85): buckets re-based to 125.53. The 2w range bucket is cut by 6 and the quarter buckets shift toward down. Two of the three parts of my earlier bearish 'systemic' trigger have fired (VIX above 25, HY OAS above 3.5). The third, NFCI above -0.40, has not (-0.48). Confidence is raised from 25 to 30 because macro and sector factors now explain a large share of the move instead of none.

Before vs after the print: the 2026-11-17 results beat, and the stock fell anyway. After the print, the driver widened from stock-specific to a risk-off across the whole AI complex (SOX -17.13% for the week, AMD -13.25% on Friday). Friday's SEC/accounting report is idiosyncratic and outside my lane, but it landed during a macro risk-off, which magnified it.

Ladder pacing (macro view; proposal only, owner approval required, no order to be placed or executed): (1) Catalysts are clustered: 2026-11-25 PCE, 2026-12-01..04 ISM/NFP and 2026-12-09/10 FOMC/CPI. I suggest the owner consider spreading any tranches across time as well as price, with no more than about a third of the remaining weight committed before the 2026-12-09/10 FOMC/CPI pair. A hawkish outcome there is the main macro route to the down bucket (below 112.98). (2) At VIX 35.9 and one-day moves of 14%, price zones planned under VIX 19 are too tightly spaced. I suggest the chair have zone spacing checked against current ATR so that several levels cannot fill in a single session. (3) Possible macro confirmations for heavier tranches: VIX back below 25, HY OAS stable below 3.5, S5TH turning up. The trade-off is that waiting for confirmation usually means buying higher after capitulation lows. A time-and-price split covers both cases. (4) Per the 2026-11-15 chair record, the price now sits inside the previously proposed L4 zone (124-128). Whether the TB2 pause still applies, and whether the SEC report triggers any thesis break, are the chair's rulings, not mine.
The 2w measurement close is Fri 2026-12-04, NFP day. A strong NFP is ambiguous in this regime: good for growth, bad for hike odds. Expect a large single-day swing on the deciding day.
Cross-domain: no thesis break is evidenced by macro. ISM 55.5 does not point to hyperscaler capex cuts (TB4 belongs to fundamentals/narrative).

Pre-mortem: if this is badly wrong in three months, the likely reason is that VIX 35.9 and a worst-since-2020 Nasdaq week marked a capitulation low (as in past VIX spikes), and the AI complex rebounded hard while the Fed held. My extra down weight would then be recency/availability bias. The other failure is a hawkish FOMC/CPI on 2026-12-09/10 that turns the risk-off into credit stress (HY above 4), which would make even my 34% quarter-down too low.
No orders suggested; ladder changes only with owner approval.
